title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-5
notes:
West leads the ♦J against 4♥. After ruffing the second diamond lead, South has 2 more certain losers, the ♥A and the ♥K. Therefore, it is necessary to assume that the spade finesse is working. Dummy has 2 entries in clubs which South can use to finesse spades twice.

Trump should be drawn first. Ideally, South would like to lead hearts twice from the North hand towards South's honours. Unfortunately, both of dummy's entries must be used to finesse spades. South must lead hearts out of the closed hand.

South should start by leading a low heart, not the ♥Q or ♥J. If trumps split 2-2, South's play does not matter as only 2 heart tricks will be lost. South will have no chance if West or East has all 4 hearts.

The 3-1 trump breaks are critical. Leading low on the first round will work when either defender has a singleton honour in hearts. There are four ways this can happen. When hearts are played by leading the ♥J or ♥Q first, only two of the 3-1 breaks can be picked up (singleton ♥10 in either hand).

Starting a low trump from South, catering to four 3-1 breaks, is thus twice as likely to succeed as starting with the ♥Q or ♥J.
